doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A month with Basie replacing Buck Clayton
summary: When Basie came through Dayton, Young went on the road for about a month filling in for Buck Clayton.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well it says here…that you went on tour briefly with Count Basie‘s band in June ‘42. Did you go on tour with Count Basie‘s band in June of 1942? Well, when they came to Dayton, when Count Basie‘s band came to Dayton, did you perform with them?
Let me think, let me see now. Yes, I was in there in ‘42. Oh, I think…yes, that‘s when they came through and I, and I think they needed a trumpet player because…what‘s his name? Buck Clayton…

Buck Clayton had to have his tonsils out or something. So I went and stayed with the band till Buck Clayton come back. Because they asked me would I come and join the band. And I told them I‘m going to replace Buck Clayton, that ain‘t my chair. They said don‘t worry about it, come on in the band anyway. Because Buck Clayton was the soloist in that band, Buck Clayton and Harry Edison, you know what I‘m saying. So but I‘m a first trumpet player, so they wanted me in there anyway. So I went on the road with them for about a month till Buck Clayton got well and came back. So then I went back home, that‘s when I went back home and went on to California.
